title: Setting `metricName` in trigger metadata is deprecated

detection.reason: checked on the composite <type>/<key> of every projected trigger; aws-cloudwatch, huawei-cloudeye and azure-monitor are NOT listed: there `metricName` is the cloud metric the scaler queries (required), not the HPA metric name — leave it there (E2 audit 2026-10-27)

remediation: Remove `metricName` from the metadata of each trigger named; KEDA generates the HPA metric name itself (`s<index>-<type>-<...>`). Anything that reads the HPA's external metric by its custom name (dashboards, `kubectl get hpa` scripts) must switch to the generated name. The key is ignored from 2.12 on. Exception: aws-cloudwatch and huawei-cloudeye REQUIRE `metricName` (it names the CloudWatch / Cloud Eye metric to query — the scaler errors `metric name not given` without it) and azure-monitor uses it the same way; leave those alone.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type | IN("azure-monitor","aws-cloudwatch","huawei-cloudeye") | not)) | select(((.metadata // {}) | has("metricName"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row sets metricName as an HPA metric name; the three cloud-metric scalers are skipped on purpose

title: Prometheus `cortexOrgID` is refused — the scaler errors until it is replaced by `customHeaders`

detection.reason: checked on the ScaledObject/ScaledJob triggers the agent projects (trigger type + metadata KEY names, never values) — a key supplied through a TriggerAuthentication or an environment variable is not a metadata key and is not scanned

quote: **Prometheus Scaler**: `cortexOrgId` metadata deprecated in favor of custom headers (#4208)
remediation: KEDA 2.10 does not merely deprecate `cortexOrgID`: pkg/scalers/prometheus_scaler.go returns the error "cortexOrgID is deprecated, please use customHeaders instead" whenever the key is present, so every prometheus trigger named stops producing metrics after the hop. Replace it with `customHeaders: X-Scope-OrgID=<tenant>` before upgrading. The error fires only when the value is non-empty; the key was always read case-sensitively as `cortexOrgID`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh,scaledjobs.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.triggers[]? | select((.type == "prometheus") and (.metadata // {} | has("cortexOrgID"))) | "\($o.kind) \($o.metadata.namespace // "-")/\($o.metadata.name) trigger=\(.type)"'  # each row is a prometheus trigger the 2.10 scaler refuses outright
coversNotes: docs scalers/prometheus.md: `cortexOrgID` - DEPRECATED: This parameter is deprecated as of KEDA…

title: New admission webhook rejects cpu/memory triggers whose target containers set no resource request

detection.reason: the check joins a ScaledObject trigger to the resource requests of the containers in its scaleTargetRef workload; the projection carries both halves but no rule predicate can join two kinds

quote: the scaledobject has a cpu trigger but the container %s doesn't have the cpu request defined
remediation: KEDA 2.10 introduces the keda-admission-webhooks Deployment (chart `webhooks.enabled`, on by default). On every UPDATE of a ScaledObject with a cpu or memory trigger it now rejects the object unless each container of the scaled workload declares the matching request (`resources.requests.cpu` / `.memory`). Existing objects keep running until someone edits them — add the requests to the workloads behind the ScaledObjects named, or set `metadata.containerName` to the one container that has them.
verifyCommand: kubectl get scaledobjects.keda.sh -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.triggers[]? | .type] | any(. == "cpu" or . == "memory")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) target=\(.spec.scaleTargetRef.kind // "Deployment")/\(.spec.scaleTargetRef.name) triggers=\([.spec.triggers[] | select(.type == "cpu" or .type == "memory") | .type] | join(","))"'  # for each row check that every container of the target sets requests for the listed resources
coversNotes: ScaledObject webhook: the scaledobject has a memory trigger but the container %s doesn't have the memory requ…

title: New admission webhook rejects a ScaledObject whose workload is already scaled by another HPA or ScaledObject

detection.reason: whether a second HorizontalPodAutoscaler or ScaledObject targets the same workload is a join across objects the projection does not make

quote: the workload '%s' of type '%s' is already managed by the ScaledObject '%s'
remediation: From 2.10 the admission webhook refuses to create or update a ScaledObject when a HorizontalPodAutoscaler KEDA does not own, or another ScaledObject, already targets the same workload. Before upgrading, delete the hand-written HPA (KEDA creates and owns its own) or remove the duplicate ScaledObject; otherwise the next edit of the ScaledObject is rejected.
verifyCommand: kubectl get hpa -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.metadata.labels // {})["scaledobject.keda.sh/name"] == null) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) -> \(.spec.scaleTargetRef.kind)/\(.spec.scaleTargetRef.name)"'  # each row is an HPA KEDA does not own; a ScaledObject on the same target is rejected by the 2.10 webhook
coversNotes: ScaledObject webhook: the workload '%s' of type '%s' is already managed by the hpa '%s'

title: Scaler connections require TLS 1.2 or newer

detection.reason: which endpoints the scalers talk to, and the TLS versions those endpoints offer, are not in the collected projection

quote: **General**: Use TLS1.2 as minimum TLS version (#4193)
remediation: From 2.10 KEDA's scaler clients refuse TLS 1.0 and 1.1 (tls_config.go v2.10.0: minimum `tls.VersionTLS12`). A scaler whose source (a self-hosted Prometheus, a RabbitMQ management API, …) still offers only TLS 1.0/1.1 fails after the hop. Upgrade that endpoint, or as a stop-gap set `KEDA_HTTP_MIN_TLS_VERSION` to `TLS11` or `TLS10` on the keda-operator (Helm `env`).
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[].image | test("kedacore/keda(:|@|$)")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) KEDA_HTTP_MIN_TLS_VERSION=\([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name == "KEDA_HTTP_MIN_TLS_VERSION") | .value] | join(","))"'  # the operator; an empty value means TLS 1.2 is the floor
